Let \(S_n(y)\) be the number of real \(x\) such that \(f^n(x)=y\).

Since \(f(x)=y\) has real solutions exactly when \(y\ge -1\), with one solution if \(y=-1\) and two if \(y>-1\):

\[
S_1(3)=2,\quad S_1(-1)=1,\quad S_1(1)=2.
\]

Then
\[
S_2(3)=S_1(3)+S_1(-1)=2+1=3,
\]
\[
S_2(-1)=S_1(1)=2.
\]
Also \(f(x)=1\iff x=1\pm\sqrt2\), so
\[
S_2(1)=S_1(1+\sqrt2)+S_1(1-\sqrt2)=2+2=4.
\]

Thus
\[
S_3(3)=S_2(3)+S_2(-1)=3+2=5,
\]
\[
S_3(-1)=S_2(1)=4.
\]

Since \(f^4(c)=3\) iff \(f^3(c)=3\) or \(f^3(c)=-1\), and these cannot overlap, the total is

\[
5+4=9.
\]

\[
\boxed{9}
\]
